transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Hi, doctor. Thanks for seeing me. Well, what brings me in is... I just keep making these really dumb mistakes at work. I supervise a sales team, and I've been messing up our sales reports. Like, I'll copy the wrong numbers right off the team dashboard, or I'll just completely miss a line in a procedure I'm supposed to be checking. The frustrating part is that it happens even when I thought I had already gone over everything.
How long has this pattern of making mistakes at work been going on? Did this start suddenly, or has it always been something you've struggled with?

It's been a real problem since I moved into the supervisor role... about a year and two months ago, I guess. I mean, I've always had my moments, but it really started impacting my work when I got promoted to this position. The details just slip past me now.
Besides these mistakes at work, how has your mood been lately? Have you been feeling down, sad, anxious, or worried about things?

No, not really. I mean, my mood is generally fine. I'm not feeling down or depressed or anything like that. 

I guess I get a little stressed or... just frustrated with myself when I realize I've messed up another report, but overall I wouldn't say I'm an anxious person. It's really just these mistakes at work that are bothering me. Other than that, I feel okay.

Before this supervisor role started about 14 months ago, did you experience any significant head injuries, illnesses, infections, surgeries, or major life events? Or have you noticed any other changes in your physical health around that time?

No, nothing like that. I haven't had any head injuries or surgeries or anything major happen. My health has been pretty normal, honestly. I haven't really noticed any physical changes either, just the issues with my focus at work.

Looking back to before you got promoted to supervisor, when you were in your previous role, did you have similar problems with missing details or making careless mistakes, or is this really something new that started with the promotion?

I mean... I wouldn't say it's completely new. Even in my old role, I'd sometimes rush through things and miss a detail here or there. But it wasn't a big deal back then. The tasks were more straightforward, so if I made a mistake, it was easy to catch or fix. 

So, yeah, I've always been a little prone to careless errors, I guess. It just wasn't causing me actual problems until I got this promotion and the workload got more complicated.

Outside of work, in your personal life—like managing your finances, household tasks, hobbies, or social commitments—do you also find yourself making careless mistakes or having trouble focusing on details, or is this really just something that happens at work?

Honestly, I haven't really noticed it being an issue outside of work. I mean, my wife usually handles the bills and the budget, so I don't really have to deal with the fine details there. And with stuff around the house or my hobbies... I don't know, it just doesn't feel like there's the same kind of pressure to get every little detail perfect, you know? So, yeah, I'd say it's really just at work where it's causing a problem.

Going back to when you were in school or earlier in your career, before this supervisor job—did teachers or earlier supervisors ever comment on you being careless, disorganized, or having trouble paying attention to details?

Yeah, actually, I was like this as a kid too. My mom still brings it up sometimes. She says she used to get notes from my teachers back in elementary school all the time. They'd say I was always rushing through my work, or I'd lose my homework before I could even turn it in. 

And it wasn't just the work, either. They'd write that I talked out of turn a lot, or that I couldn't just stay in my seat without someone reminding me to sit down. So, I guess it's been going on for a long time, really.
